long_biography.plain_text:
The Takis Pattichis Museum of Industrial Pharmacy turned Charalambos Pattihis's family history into a public account of medicines manufacturing in Cyprus. Created by the foundation he established with his wife, Elena, it preserves production machinery, laboratory equipment and the export legacy of his father, Remedica founder Takis Pattichis.

Pattihis brought his own technical education to the company, earning degrees in chemistry with management, pharmaceutical technology and business administration. More than two decades in the industry led to leadership of Remedica and the founding presidency of the Cyprus Pharmaceutical Manufacturers' Association. Through the Charalambos & Elena Pattihis Foundation, he now supports welfare, education and culture, while the museum gives students and visitors practical access to Cyprus's industrial pharmaceutical history.

uncertainties.detail: The upstream record is securely resolved to the Cypriot Remedica executive born in April 1964. Official sources distinguish Charalambos Pattihis from his father, Remedica founder Christakis 'Takis' Pattichis, and from other similar Cypriot names. The father's surname is often rendered Pattichis while the son's records consistently use Pattihis; that transliteration difference is preserved and does not justify altering either identity.

Ascendis's transaction circular identifies Pattihis as legal and beneficial owner of PCHL, which held 55.562% of Remedica, and as legal owner of Goldbond. It allocates substantial cash, shares, deferred consideration and earn-out rights to him. Healthcare therefore rests on direct personal control and sale economics rather than his chief-executive title or family name alone.

Takis Pattichis founded the business, Charalambos succeeded as chief executive, and Charalambos later controlled and economically benefited from the majority holding sold to Ascendis. These facts meet the family-transfer test. No reviewed source states that the Remedica shares were inherited or identifies the transfer instrument, so Inherited and Inherited and expanded are not used even though Charalambos materially helped grow the company.

The Remedica holding was sold and Pattihis is no longer its chief executive. Companies House records show active private company interests, but their combined assets, sectors and importance to his current wealth are not public. Healthcare is therefore an explicit origin-sector fallback for Primary Industry. Wealth Relationship remains Unknown because Investor, Family office principal and Passive asset owner each lack evidence of a current principal-wealth mandate.

The source biography calls Pattihis 58 and describes him as Remedica's current chief executive. Age language dates immediately, and Andrew Bird became Remedica chief executive in April 2025. The replacement removes transient counts and links, changes the executive role to historical, and retains the enduring family-business, ownership, sale and foundation story.

The existing April 1964 birth details, Cypriot nationality and Cyprus residence are corroborated by Ascendis and Companies House records. No authoritative source reviewed provides the birth day, a birthplace, a middle name or a secondary nationality, so those researchable blanks remain unfilled.

The official Charalambos & Elena Pattihis Foundation domain is proposed as a Company Website because Pattihis co-founded the organisation and continues to represent it. No identity-secure personal LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, X, YouTube, TikTok or personal website was found. Exact-name Forbes profile-path and wider-domain searches found no dedicated profile.

Pharmaceuticals is the sole minimum-useful active tag because Pattihis's former controlling stake and long operating mandate at Remedica satisfy its wealth-producing and substantial-operations contract. It is marked former but defining after the company sale and chief-executive departure. Philanthropy domains and the family foundation are retained in narrative rather than converted into generic or named-entity tags.

The short biography explains the family-founded company, controlling stake, sale and foundation. The long profile instead develops the museum, technical education, pharmaceutical-association role and current charitable programme.
